html:
The Darien scheme was an attempt by the Kingdom of Scotland to found a colony on the isthmus of Panama, at Darién, from 1698 to 1700. It ended in disaster.

The Company of Scotland raised perhaps a fifth of the country's wealth from people of every rank. It planned a trading post, New Caledonia, to link the Atlantic and Pacific. About 2,500 settlers sailed in two expeditions. Disease, hunger and bad planning killed most of them; English colonies were ordered not to help, and Spanish forces besieged the second group, which surrendered in 1700.

The loss ruined many Scots. When England offered, in the Act of Union of 1707, to pay off the company's investors, it helped win support for joining the two kingdoms. The dream of a passage across Panama was realised two centuries later in the Panama Canal.
